I build internal tools and workflow automations with **Claude in the loop** — and I treat AI as a tool to supervise, not a shortcut to skip thinking.

The model writes roughly 90% of the keystrokes. The remaining 10% is where the work actually is — scoping the problem, choosing what's worth shipping, debugging what the model got wrong, and making sure I still understand every line that ends up in `main`.

Second year of DAW in Barcelona (2025–2027). Coursework fundamentals are done **deliberately AI-free**: if I can't write it myself, I don't claim it. Most repositories are private while in development; I'm happy to walk through any of them line by line in a call.

<img alt="AI engineering — Claude, past autocomplete. How a feature actually gets built: I own the scope and the merge, the agents do the legwork in between. I scope and decide; Claude Code plans and orchestrates parallel subagents: explore (maps the codebase); build (test first, small slices); review (fresh context, fresh eyes); only what I understand reaches main. Context it starts with: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, Skills, MCP servers, Memory, Context engineering. Guardrails I keep: Evals vs hand-written truth, Schema-validated output, Model reads, code decides, I review every merge." src="assets/ai-engineering.svg" width="100%">
